provenance: Hand-written for the 2026-09-28 mock demo day by the inVision U dev team. Not generated by a model and not any applicant's session. The numbers below are illustrative and, like every simulation result, carry weight zero.

messages.content: Hi Arman! I heard your team has a problem with the poster. What happened?

Hi! So our science poster is due on Friday and Dana was supposed to do the drawings. But she did nothing for a whole week and she doesn't answer in our group chat! Timur says he'll just do her drawings himself. Aru says we should talk to Dana first, even if we're late. What would you do?

That sounds stressful. I would talk to Dana first, but today, not on Thursday night. Maybe something is going on with her that you don't know about. If you just redo her part, she never gets the chance to explain, and Timur ends up doing two jobs.
Oh. But what if she's just lazy? Then talking is a waste of time and the poster will be late.

Maybe. But you don't know that yet, and it only takes five minutes to ask. You could say: 'Dana, we're worried about Friday, is everything okay? Can you still do the drawings?' If she says she can't, then the team decides together who takes them, not just Timur alone.
But if we talk to Dana, won't she be angry at us? I don't want her to think we're telling on her.

Good question. That's why you ask her kindly and just between you, not in front of the whole class and not by going to the teacher first. You're not blaming her, you're asking. If she still doesn't answer by tomorrow, then you tell the teacher what happened, together as a team.
Okay... so first we ask Dana nicely, and if she can't do it we share the drawings? Not only Timur?
Exactly. Split the drawings so it's fair for Timur too. And maybe give Dana a smaller part she can still finish, so she's still part of the team.
Oh! That's like when my friend was sick and we gave him the easy part of our game. I'll message Dana today!

score.summary: In this simulation the candidate advised talking to the teammate early and kindly before redistributing work, and answered each of the child's worries directly. They considered the absent teammate, the overloaded teammate and the deadline, and gave a concrete fallback if the conversation did not help.

quiz_answers.question: What did they say you should do about Dana?
quiz_answers.answer: Ask her nicely, just me and her, if everything is okay and if she can still do the drawings.

quiz_answers.question: Why is that better than the other choice?
quiz_answers.answer: Because maybe something happened to her, and if Timur does it all he has two jobs and that's not fair.

quiz_answers.question: What should you do if Dana still doesn't help?
quiz_answers.answer: Share the drawings with the whole team and tell the teacher together. And give Dana a small part.
